activities.caption: pair each listener with the merge
activities.name: pipaFilterMatch

config.prompt: The first year of life sorted everyone's hearing — pair each listener with what gets merged:

pairs.right: Mandarin tones — pitch is not contrastive at home
vowel length, heard as style rather than meaning

config.why: Adults are not stuck: the filter is retrainable — but the training must target perception itself, which is why "just listen a lot" is slow and "discriminate these two, get feedback" is fast.

activities.anchor: hear one, identify which, get told immediately
activities.caption: bet on the one-voice shortcut
activities.name: pipaVariabilityPredict

config.q: You drill ship/sheep against one flawless recording until you always get it right. What does the high-variability research say about that plan?
choices: It is the fastest route — consistency builds the category
It generalises worse than the same drills across many different speakers
It makes no difference how many voices you train on
config.why: One voice is an exemplar; ten are a distribution. And perception leads production — ear work is not warm-up, it is the first half of the skill.

activities.anchor: that single decoy gets most learners the sound in minutes
activities.caption: fill the recipes — say X, change Y
activities.name: pipaRecipeCloze

config.text: French "u" /y/: say English "ee" and %%round%% your lips without moving the tongue; French "j" /ʒ/: say "sh" and switch your %%voice%% on mid-sound; Spanish rolled rr: tongue tip lightly touching the alveolar ridge, %%relaxed%%, blown past by airflow.
config.hint: Each recipe changes exactly one variable from a sound you already make.

activities.anchor: a position that feels strange is usually the correct one
activities.caption: find the line the feelings would love
activities.name: pipaMotorSpot

config.prompt: One line of this training note inverts the research — click it:
lines: Train it like a motor skill: short daily sets, high repetitions.
Progression runs isolated sound → syllable → word → full-speed sentence.
The mouth's habits respond to volume and consistency, not to intensity.
If a position feels strange, you are doing it wrong — go back to what feels natural.
Natural-feeling positions are usually your first language reaching over.
config.correction: Strange usually means new — and correct; natural usually means the first language reaching over.
config.why: The mouth's proprioception lies; the recording is the honest witness.

activities.anchor: listeners judge and understand speech more through
activities.caption: drag the divider — vowels, then melody
activities.name: pipaProsodyCompare

config.prompt: Two learners walk into a conversation — drag the divider:

before.label: Careful vowels, first-language rhythm
before.text: Harder to follow despite the careful vowels — the home rhythm gives it away.

after.label: Thick accent, accurate melody
after.text: Easier to follow despite the accent — the accurate melody carries it.

config.why: Mark where the stressed syllables fall, copy whole-sentence tunes — questions rise, lists march, corrections fall — and imitate speed; that is exactly what shadowing drills.

activities.anchor: climbs from chance to reliable within ten or so sessions
activities.caption: line up the four weeks, perception first
activities.name: pipaRepairOrder

config.prompt: One contrast, four weeks — order the repair:
items: Week 1 — perception only: minimal pairs across at least five speakers, immediate feedback
Week 2 — articulation: the IPA recipe drilled in syllables, then words, with daily record-and-compare
Week 3 — sentences: shadow the pair-heavy lines so the contrast survives speed
Week 4 — conversation: use the pair in tutoring, ask for flags, log what happens
config.why: Fifteen minutes a day, one contrast — then functional load points where the next cycles go, because the vowel inventory is where comprehension breaks hardest.

activities.anchor: the perception-first protocol works across every pair
activities.caption: pair each learner with the fight
activities.name: pipaTroubleMatch

config.prompt: Trouble spots by language pair — pair the learner with the predictable fight:

pairs.right: tone, and the aspirated/unaspirated distinction English treats as allophonic

pairs.left: English speakers learning French or German
pairs.right: the front rounded vowels (u, ü) — no rounded-front category at home
the twelve-plus vowel inventory — five at home

config.why: The pattern is always the same — rebuild the category first, and the habit follows.

activities.anchor: where the eye catches what the untrained ear cannot
activities.caption: drag the divider — bare audio, then transcript
activities.name: pipaToolsCompare

config.prompt: The loop-closer in the toolkit — drag the divider:

before.label: Audio alone
before.text: You are left unsure what was said — every mishearing stays a mystery.

after.label: Audio plus transcript
after.text: Every mishearing becomes a data point — the exact mismatch between what you heard and what was said.

config.why: The tools do not teach; they make the feedback loop possible — and the loop is the teacher.
